Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 2. Routine and fun
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Corporate culture
- Materials: Office-scene picture, collocation cards, meeting agenda, COSYmanuals 'work collocations' and 'present simple' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• understand basic office dynamics and collocations
• talk about work hours, teams, and projects
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles present simple, time expressions, and daily routine.

Next lesson: This completes the A1 general course lessons in this set.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

team — a group who work or play together. Example: Our team has five people.
colleague — a person you work with. Example: My colleague is very helpful.
meeting — a time when people talk about work. Example: We have a meeting at ten.
project — a planned piece of work. Example: We are working on a new project.
deadline — the time by which work must finish. Example: The deadline is Friday.
email — a message sent by computer. Example: I send an email every morning.
manager — a person who leads a team. Example: The manager has a meeting.
office — a place where people work. Example: I work in an office.
company — a business organisation. Example: She works for a big company.
schedule — a plan of times and activities. Example: My schedule is very busy.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I have a meeting at ten. (talking about a meeting)
• I send emails to my colleagues. (talking about communication)
• We work on a project together. (talking about teamwork)
• The deadline is Friday. (talking about deadlines)
• My colleague is very helpful. (describing a colleague)
• Our team meets every Monday. (describing a routine)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a group who work or play together'?
Which word means 'a person you work with'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Work word stress and the /k/ sound in 'colleague'

colleague /ˈkɒliːɡ/ — silent ue
meeting /ˈmiːtɪŋ/ — long /iː/
project /ˈprɒdʒekt/ — stress the first syllable
deadline /ˈdedlaɪn/ — stress the first syllable
Listen and repeat:
I have a meeting at ten. We work on a project together.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use common verb + noun combinations to talk about work.

Form:
Work collocations: have a meeting, make a call, do a project, take a break, send an email, meet a deadline.

Examples:
• I have a meeting every Monday.
• She sends emails to her team.
• We do a project together.
• He takes a break at noon.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I ___ a meeting at ten.
She ___ a phone call.
We ___ a project this week.
He ___ a break at noon.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I have ... (a meeting / a call) at ...
• I send ... (an email / a report) to ...
• We do ... (a project / a task) together.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What do you do at work or school?
• How often do you have meetings?
• Who do you send emails to?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your work or study day with collocations.
• Write three sentences about a colleague's work day.
Reading: Corporate culture

In our company, the team meets every Monday morning. I have a meeting with my manager at ten. My colleagues and I work on a new project. We send emails and take breaks together. The deadline is Friday, so we are busy. Our office is friendly and quiet. I like my team and my work.
When does the team meet?
When is the deadline?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Do you have a meeting today?
B: Yes, I have a meeting at ten with my manager.
A: What are you working on?
B: We are working on a new project. The deadline is Friday.
A: Do you send many emails?
B: Yes, I send emails to my colleagues every day.
What time is the meeting?
When is the deadline?
Speaking task: Describe your work or study day to your partner. Use five work collocations.

• What do you do at work or school?
• How often do you have meetings?
• Who do you send emails to?
• Do you work in a team?
• What is a good manager like?
Role-play: You are a new employee. Ask a colleague about the team, meetings, projects, and deadlines.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about your work or study routine using work collocations.
Model: I have ... I send ... We work on ... The deadline is ...
